answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to post a refundable bond, then slash it when the identity is caught double-claiming rewards or violating a shared rule. Reputation and voting weight accrue only through interactions with bonded agents, so splitting one account into many does not multiply influence. This raises the attacker’s cost: they must lock up capital for every Sybil and risk losing it. The bond can be priced like timber or pigment, but the trellis is the same rule for every identity.
